summary: Tigris & Euphrates is Knizia's abstract civilization classic where players place tiles to grow kingdoms led by four types of leaders, with your final score determined by your weakest of the four color categories, forcing balanced development. Conflicts between adjacent kingdoms are resolved by leader strength and can wipe out large swaths of tiles, making it a tense, cutthroat game beneath its calm exterior.
praised: brilliant 'your weakest category counts' scoring twist
deep, elegant rules with minimal luck
criticised: steep learning curve for an abstract game
can feel harsh or swingy for newer players when a kingdom collapses
dry presentation that undersells its depth

interaction.kind: open conflict and territorial tile placement
interaction.detail: All tiles and leaders are placed on one shared board, and kingdoms merging or leaders clashing directly destroys opponents' tiles and points, so nearly the entire game state is contested rather than private.

scoring.why: Only your lowest-scoring color category counts at the end, so the winner is whoever balances all four leader types rather than maxing any single one.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by carefully bringing all four of your victory point colors up together while using conflicts to weaken opponents' weakest categories even further.
